newsitem.title: GERMANY: Britannia Airways to launch German flights.
newsitem.headline: Britannia Airways to launch German flights.

text.p: British charter airline group Britannia Airways said on Monday it would take on established German charter airlines Condor and LTU on their home turf with new service from Germany starting in the autumn.
Britannia Airways chairman Richard Manley said the airline would base its operations in either Munich or Berlin and will initially concentrate on charter flights to the Caribbean.
Manley said the new subsidiary would make a profit in its first year and that some eight aircraft would be put into operation within three to five years.
Although Condor, a unit of Lufthansa AG, and LTU already have a strong hold on the German market, Manley said Britannia would succeed in Germany because it can operate more efficiently.

He said the airline has signed a long-term greement with travel agency Frosch Touristik International under which Britannia will sell entire flights to Frosch and not individual seats directly to the public, as do LTU and Condor.

Manley said key positions of Britannia's operations in Germany will be staffed by Germans and will initially employ 200 people. Within five years, he said Britannia expected to employ another 500 people in the country.
Britannia Airways, a unit of Thomson Travel Group, carried 7.5 million passengers in 1996.
